message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so a direct-match exists. Among them, PGS000753 provides the cleanest PRS-specific evidence in the visible metadata: it reports an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), avoiding reliance on potentially covariate-inflated full-model AUROC/C-index. Competing models mainly report full-model discrimination metrics (e.g., AUROC/C-index) with varying/unknown covariates, which are not clearly PRS-only and therefore are less comparable for ranking; the one explicit PRS-comparable metric (PGS001784 Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out 0.014661) comes from a portability/framework-style paper, which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused alternatives unless clearly superior on endpoint+metrics. Remaining limitation: the pool lacks consistently reported PRS-only AUROC/R2 across candidates, and several records have unknown covariates or only full-model metrics, so the choice cannot be made with high confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 4 candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target (alcohol dependence) via alcohol use disorder / problematic alcohol use, with endpoint fidelity supported by phenotyping_reported being Alcohol use disorder (DSM-5 criteria count) for PGS000201/PGS000202 and Alcohol use disorder for PGS002738/PGS002739. Among these, PGS002738 is the most directly aligned at the concept level (trait_efo = alcohol dependence) and provides the strongest visible discriminative evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample. However, confidence is not high because key comparable PRS-only metrics (AUC/R2) are missing across candidates, covariates are listed as Unknown for PGS002738 (limiting comparability), and PGS000201 reports only a small incremental ΔR² (0.01192) on a related but not exact EFO mapping (alcohol dependence measurement), making the overall evidence set supportive but not definitive."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000704","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned disease endpoints in trait_reported/phenotyping_reported. PGS000704 is preferred because it has (i) endpoint-fidelity consistent with the target (Alcoholic cirrhosis), (ii) a structurally strong genome-wide approach (snpnet multi-PRS) with very large variant coverage (183,271), and (iii) performance reported with relatively clean/basic covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs) alongside a representative European validation record (C-index 0.711; HR per SD 1.18). The main limitation is that the available discrimination metric is a full-model C-index (not explicitly PGS-only), and the HR indicates only modest PRS signal; competing models report stronger risk stratification (e.g., PGS001777 OR top vs bottom quintiles 6.18; PGS004913 OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4) but are based on much smaller SNP sets and/or have less clear covariate reporting (PGS001777 covariates unknown, 3-variant score). Given these comparability gaps and lack of explicit PRS-only AUC/R² across candidates, the direct-match choice is supported but not high-certainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris), with several endpoint-faithful phenotypes (e.g., ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, and doctor-diagnosed angina). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet UKB framework family (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.59) and PGS R2 (~0.012–0.013) plus incremental AUROC, enabling more interpretable PRS-only comparison than candidates that report only full-model C-index/AUROC or only an OR. Within that family, PGS001262 has the strongest reported full-model AUROC (0.80729) and the highest incremental AUROC (0.0098) with similar basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and an endpoint that is still a direct diagnosis construct (“Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina”). However, confidence is limited because (1) this snpnet family comes from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework paper (a known generalizability risk per the provided domain guidance), and (2) several newer ICD10/PheCode-based candidates (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527 and PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057) show stronger effect sizes (OR ~1.43–1.49) and/or higher full-model C-index (~0.76) but lack clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics, making cross-study ranking non-comparable from the visible evidence alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. Among them, PGS001267 provides the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.72651, with CI) and PGS-only R² (0.09877), plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Competing UKB portability models (PGS001876, PGS002089) lack AUROC/R² and only report partial correlation, making them harder to compare on discrimination. The Taiwanese EAS-only models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation N (n=1,298), so their AUC is less interpretable as PRS-only performance. Main limitation: PGS001267 comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (\"across 813 traits\"), which domain guidance flags as a generalizability risk; PGS001268 is a near-tie on metrics but uses a time-to-event endpoint, adding endpoint-specificity ambiguity for generic disease-risk use. Hence a direct match exists but the best choice is not unequivocally high-quality from the visible evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) and several related aortic valve measurement scores (PGS005255, PGS005256); hypertrophic cardiomyopathy scores are not direct matches to the target trait. PGS005252 has the strongest endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported = incident aortic stenosis cases) and provides the richest visible performance evidence among the direct aortic stenosis models, including a reported C-index of 0.87 and HR=1.92 in a large European evaluation (n=446,895). A key limitation is that the reported discrimination metric appears to be a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (multiple comorbidities/risk factors), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, reducing comparability versus PGS005254 (which uses only basic covariates but lacks AUC/C-index). Given the available metadata, PGS005252 remains the best-supported direct-match choice, but confidence is moderated by the lack of PRS-only performance metrics and covariate-heavy evaluation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the exact target trait (arthritis; EFO: arthritis) are present, notably PGS001135 (\"Arthritis (nos)\") and the Commun Biol \"Other arthritis\" models (PGS004477, PGS004547). PGS001135 has the strongest endpoint fidelity for the generic target (phenotyping_reported: \"Arthritis (nos)\") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) alongside a European-selected validation record (full-model AUROC=0.67424). In contrast, PGS004477/PGS004547 match the EFO but use a narrower/administrative endpoint label (\"M13 (Other arthritis)\") and report only an OR without AUC/R2, limiting comparability and making them harder to justify as clearly superior from the visible evidence. Confidence is Moderate because the direct-match pool includes multiple arthritis-EFO models with incomplete and non-uniform performance reporting, preventing a high-certainty dominance claim."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002727","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for asthma are present (many models with trait_efo=asthma). Among the listed options, PGS002727 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is disease-focused (publication: “Multiancestral polygenic risk score for pediatric asthma”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with large variant coverage (668,286), and reports relatively strong PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) alongside a moderate full-model AUROC (0.66). Key limitation: its phenotyping_reported is explicitly pediatric asthma (endpoint restriction vs generic asthma target), and covariates are listed as Unknown, reducing comparability; additionally, several other direct-match models show similar full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS001344 full-model AUROC 0.666 with basic covariates) but lack similarly strong per-SD effect-size reporting, making the overall choice not unequivocal from metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on therapy-specific “paradoxical eczema” in biologic-treated psoriasis patients rather than generic atopic eczema risk, making them weaker direct matches despite reporting AUROC ~0.57–0.59 or ORs. PGS001773 targets “moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis” and reports very high full-model AUROC (0.93) and R² (0.49), but these are full-model metrics with multiple non-genetic covariates (age/sex/parental ethnicity) and no PRS-only metrics, so the apparent performance is not clearly attributable to the PRS and looks like a potential comparability/packaging issue. Between the two incident atopic dermatitis models (PGS002755 and PGS004587), both use similar covariates and have large European evaluation; PGS002755 is structurally stronger (PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants) and reports an HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 (1.123–1.391), which is modest but the strongest directly comparable effect-size evidence among the incident-endpoint options shown. Confidence is not high because no candidate reports PRS-only AUROC/R² and the best-supported choice relies on limited effect-size reporting rather than clean PRS-only discrimination metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in the provided context because it is a disease-focused atrial fibrillation PRS-CS model from a large AF meta-analysis (Nat Genet; multi-cohort development listed) with a direct AF endpoint (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation) and strong reported discrimination in European validation (C-index 0.8718 with CI 0.8657–0.878) plus a per-SD HR of 1.6663. Main limitation: many other direct-match candidates also report strong full-model metrics (and most lack clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2), making cross-model comparability imperfect; additionally, PGS005168’s covariates include CHARGE-AF (a clinical risk calculator), which can inflate full-model performance and reduces certainty about standalone PRS contribution, so confidence is not high despite the strong overall evidence package."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches at the concept level (each includes atrial flutter in trait_reported/trait_efo), but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS001263 is the only model with phenotyping_reported exactly \"Atrial flutter\", whereas PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050 use the combined endpoint \"Atrial fibrillation and flutter\" (and PGS001339 is additionally time-to-event). For comparable PRS-only performance evidence, only the snpnet models (PGS001263, PGS001339) report explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²; PGS001263 has slightly higher PGS-only AUROC (0.61716 vs 0.613) and PGS-only R² (0.02517 vs 0.02447) with similar basic covariates, supporting it as the best direct atrial-flutter-specific choice. Main limitation: the selected model comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (\"across 813 traits\"), and the alternative portability-study models (PGS001841/PGS002050) use genome-wide shrinkage/penalized regression with more variants but lack directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R² in the provided metadata, preventing a high-confidence superiority claim."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ materially on endpoint fidelity. PGS000327 has phenotyping_reported = \"Autism spectrum disorder\" (direct diagnosis endpoint) and provides supportive PRS evidence via an OR per SD of 1.33 (with CI) plus an R² estimate (0.0245) from a single European validation record with basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). In contrast, PGS002790 has phenotyping_reported = \"Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)\", which is an explicit endpoint mismatch/withdrawn phenotype despite the ASD label fields, and its reported partial R² (0.00546) is weaker and less directly comparable. Overall, PGS000327 is the best-supported direct-match candidate, but confidence is limited because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUROC/R²) and the available R² values may reflect full-model/partial metrics rather than clean PRS-only performance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000452","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 20 candidates are direct matches on concept (`trait_reported`/`trait_efo` = basal cell carcinoma). Prioritizing endpoint fidelity and comparable evidence, most models use a straightforward basal cell carcinoma endpoint with only basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), which is acceptable and broadly comparable across the Cancer PRSweb sibling set (PGS000445–PGS000459). Within that coherent family, PGS000452 (GWAS Hits, 28 variants) has the strongest reported validation performance among siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), the highest/near-highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0487), and a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) plus a high top-1%-vs-rest OR 3.61—collectively supporting stronger discriminative signal than other siblings (e.g., PGS000447/448 with lower AUROC ~0.59 and smaller per-SD OR ~1.40; PGS000446 with AUROC 0.575). Although PGS000119 reports a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.64), it is from a different study family and still only provides full-model metrics (no PRS-only AUC/R²), making the small AUROC difference hard to interpret as a true PRS advantage. Key limitation: across the pool, reported AUROCs are full-model (covariate-adjusted) rather than explicitly PRS-only, so cross-model ranking certainty is constrained; thus confidence is moderate rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002032","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO concept (bilirubin metabolism disease) via trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS001824 and PGS002032 have the most endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported/trait_reported (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), whereas PGS000924 uses a broader combined endpoint and is explicitly time-to-event (“TTE disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”), which is a noted warning signal when the target is a generic disease concept. Between the two bilirubin-excretion siblings (same publication, same covariates, same reported partial-r performance), PGS002032 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far higher variant count (19,768 vs 22), which is a positive signal for capturing polygenic signal when other evidence is essentially tied. Limitation: the key PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for both PGS001824 and PGS002032, and the only reported metric is partial correlation, so the selection is driven mainly by endpoint alignment plus structural/method signals rather than directly comparable PRS discrimination evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches by trait label/EFO to bipolar disorder (broad BD, BD I, BD II) and share the same publication family, method (SDPR), and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, so transportability and method do not differentiate them. However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/weak for all three because `phenotyping_reported` fields are not bipolar disorder diagnosis endpoints (they reference cognitive/behavioral measures such as pattern comparison, DSM5 depression behavior, and sluggish cognitive tempo), which limits confidence that these are optimized/validated for bipolar disorder risk prediction despite the trait labels. Given similarly limited evidence, PGS002786 is selected only because it is the broadest concept match to the target trait (‘Bipolar disorder’ rather than subtype-specific BD I/BD II), but this is a marginal advantage and the overall evidence remains insufficient for a high-quality direct-match recommendation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct-match at the broad concept level (target: blood coagulation disease). PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (blood coagulation disease) and provides the most complete, PRS-comparable performance evidence, including explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS-only R² (0.0578) plus a European-selected validation record with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), which supports interpretability. However, its endpoint fidelity is weaker because phenotyping_reported is time-to-event (“TTE other coagulation defects”), and it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework paper (a known weaker study archetype signal in the provided domain guidance), and the score is extremely sparse (1 variant), raising concerns about capturing polygenic signal. The two alternative models (PGS001826, PGS002034) have more specific congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoints (not the same EFO as the target) and lack AUROC/R², reporting only partial correlation (~0.056) from a portability framework; between them there is no clear differentiator from the visible evidence. Given these trade-offs and framework-origin limitations across all candidates, the best pick is PGS001033 but only with low confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the provided context. Among the visible models, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is a direct breast cancer PRS with strong reported discrimination in European evaluation (AUROC 0.6625 with R² 0.0764) and an explicitly empty covariate set (covariates=0), which improves comparability versus models whose reported performance may be boosted by clinical risk calculators or extensive non-genetic covariates (e.g., BCSC risk model in PGS000028/PGS000029). It also outperforms closely related high-performing direct-match alternatives in the same 2023 multi-method evaluation family (e.g., LDpred2-auto PGS004025 AUROC ~0.6598; LDpred2.CV PGS004040 AUROC ~0.6598; PRS-CS-auto PGS004083 AUROC ~0.6553) on the visible metrics. Main limitation: the context contains many other direct-match breast cancer PRSs from different study families (e.g., PGS000007 reports full_model_auc 0.78 but with age/sex covariates; PGS001336 reports very high full_model_auc 0.8096 with covariates), and full-model AUROC values are not directly comparable to PRS-only performance; additionally, the evidence shown does not include explicit PGS-only AUROC for most candidates, so confidence is reduced despite PGS004153 being the best-supported choice from the visible, covariate-clean, directly comparable metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001301","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease at the trait_efo level, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and in whether they report PRS-comparable performance. PGS001301 is preferred because it provides explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.82867; PGS R² (no covariates)=0.14224) alongside full-model metrics and clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making its reported performance more interpretable and comparable than candidates that report only full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000040/PGS000316) or only partial correlation without AUROC/R² (e.g., PGS001856/PGS002067). The main limitation is that PGS001301 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework study (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused models; additionally, several disease-focused celiac-specific models exist here but lack PRS-only metrics, preventing a high-confidence, clearly best-supported choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001299","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). However, most models only report full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) with non-trivial covariate sets, making cross-model comparison of PRS strength uncertain. PGS001299 is best supported because it uniquely reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.55215 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00263) alongside full-model AUROC=0.76761 and incremental AUROC=0.00676, providing clearer evidence about the standalone PRS contribution than the other candidates. The main limitation is that PGS001299 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework study (snpnet, sparse 24-variant score), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable than disease-focused scores; meanwhile disease-focused alternatives (e.g., PGS003428 LDpred; PGS000073/PGS000784 GWAS-hits) lack PRS-only metrics here, preventing a high-confidence selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001174","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (or a closely overlapping composite that explicitly includes cholelithiasis). PGS001174 is preferred because it provides the clearest, PRS-comparable performance evidence in the context: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.62342, European) and PGS-only R² (0.02808), plus full-model AUROC with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), enabling more interpretable assessment than candidates that report only partial-r (PGS001861/PGS002072) or only effect sizes without AUC/R² (PGS004476/PGS004546/PGS005150). Main limitation: PGS001174 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper and uses a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals in the provided domain guidance; meanwhile, the more recent K80-specific models (PGS004476/PGS004546) and the EAS-evaluated model (PGS005150) lack comparable discrimination metrics here, preventing a high-confidence selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (chronic kidney disease), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and comparability of reported performance. PGS002237 is the most disease-focused, endpoint-specific CKD model in the set (CKD stage 3+; eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2) and comes from a CKD-focused Nat Med study explicitly aiming to predict CKD across ancestries, with multi-ancestry evaluation reported. It also reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65), supporting meaningful PRS signal. However, confidence is not high because the only discrimination metric shown is a full-model AUROC (0.78) with a relatively heavy covariate set (including hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, limiting cross-model comparability versus other direct-match options (e.g., PGS005090 reports AUROC/R² but only in African-ancestry evaluation; several 2023 ‘five biobanks’ models report modest full-model AUROCs with covariates=0 but are not clearly superior on comparable PRS-only metrics either)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001332","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among them, PGS001332 is the cleanest direct endpoint match by labels and phenotyping_reported (\"Chronic obstructive airways disease/copd\") and provides explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53971; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00235) alongside basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), making its reported PRS contribution interpretable. Competing direct COPD siblings from the same snpnet/UKB \"813 traits\" framework family (PGS001333, PGS001334) have very similar PRS-only metrics, and alternative direct COPD models from other framework/portability studies either lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (PGS001850/PGS002062) or report only limited/less comparable evidence (PGS004466/PGS004536 effect-size only with unknown covariates; PGS001783/PGS001788 report covariates-regressed-out R2 but are also framework-derived and do not clearly dominate on the visible metrics). Because the leading candidates are largely framework scores with modest PRS-only performance and near-ties across several direct COPD records, the best choice is not strongly separated, lowering confidence and making the overall direct-match recommendation sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the disease level, but they split between generic cirrhosis (PGS000726, PGS004621) and alcohol-related subtypes (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) plus one record with internally inconsistent labeling (PGS000776: method/trait suggests alcohol-related cirrhosis but phenotyping_reported describes an NAFLD at-risk incident hospitalization endpoint). For the target ‘cirrhosis of liver’ (generic), PGS004621 has the strongest endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ‘Cirrhosis’) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (1,089,806) and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is structurally favorable versus sparse GWAS-hit scores. However, the evidence remains limited because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only discrimination (most metrics shown are full-model AUROC/C-index or effect sizes), and PGS004621’s reported AUROC=0.68 is not directly comparable as PRS-only; PGS000726 is a close competitor with the same trait_efo and an OR(top vs bottom 20%)=2.26 but is a 12-variant GWS score with no AUC/R2 reported. Given these trade-offs and lack of PRS-only metrics, the best pick is supported but not definitive."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both mapped to the same target EFO and with identical endpoint fields (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported: \"Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)\") and similar evaluation context (same publication family, same covariates, same training cohort, same validation ancestry and sample size). Reported performance is essentially indistinguishable (partial-r 0.0562 vs 0.0563 with near-identical CIs; no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes shown), so the evidence is insufficient to clearly separate them. Given the tie on endpoint fidelity and metrics, PGS002034 is selected only on weak structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with many more variants than the sparse penalized regression model), but this is not strongly supported by direct comparative performance in the provided records, hence low confidence and a sub-optimal direct-match recommendation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both aligned to the target with identical trait fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Corneal dystrophy”), same publication family, similar covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and similar training/validation context. With endpoint fidelity and covariate comparability essentially tied, the main differentiators are the available PRS-comparable performance signal and structural properties: PGS002042 shows a higher selected European partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is generally supportive of capturing more polygenic signal when other fields are comparable. However, confidence is limited because neither model reports standard PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect sizes in the visible metadata (only partial-r), and both come from a UKB portability framework paper, so the evidence for a clearly strong direct-match winner is incomplete."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003725","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates are abundant (85) and many have strong endpoint alignment to coronary artery disease. Among the visible set, PGS003725 is a direct CAD endpoint (phenotyping_reported: \"Coronary artery disease\"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with substantial variant coverage (1,296,172), and reports strong PRS effect sizes (HR 1.75; OR 2.14) with multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/MAE/SAS), supporting robustness/transportability. However, confidence is limited because several other direct-match CAD scores also show strong evidence (e.g., PGS000018 reports AUROC 0.89 but is prevalent CAD with small validation n=3,309; PGS001780 reports AUROC 0.913 but is CHD and the AUROC is likely full-model; multiple candidates have unknown covariates or non-comparable full-model metrics), and many records lack clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics, making it hard to declare a single unequivocal best model from the provided metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005170","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match dementia candidates are present, including multiple models with trait_efo=dementia and dementia endpoints (e.g., PGS000929, PGS000946, PGS001827, PGS002035, PGS004281–PGS004284, PGS005170).
